newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ahmsa scraps share issue - chair.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ahmsa scraps share issue - chair.

text.p: Mexican steel giant Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) has scrapped plans to issue shares because the board does not consider it now necessary, Ahmsa's chairman said Wednesday.

"We believe we will not be carrying out the share issue that we had in mind last year and earlier this year, given the successful debt placements we have made," Xavier Autrey told an analysts' conference call.

Ahmsa recently placed $425 million in Yankee bonds and signed a syndicated export-backed credit for a further $330 million. Ahmsa intended to issue up to 55 million shares in a global offering toward the end of 1997 and also a mixed global offer for up to 100 million shares before the end of 1998.
Autrey also said Ahmsa will start using its share buy-back fund because the company believed its share prices to be undervalued.
"In the last board meeting a buy-back fund was established for 200 million pesos, now it holds 80 million pesos and we intend to use it in the next couple of days."

Ahmsa also sees liquid steel volume climbing six percent in 1997 and seven percent next year to reach 4 million tonnes annually, said Ahmsa's director general Alonso Ancira. He added the company had planned investments totaling $180 million next year in various projects. Ancira was also taking part in the conference call.
Ahmsa is also in talks with auto makers with plants in Mexico to establish long-term supply contracts, Ancira said, naming Ford Motor Co., Chrysler, General Motors and Volkswagen AG.
